findings.location: #nav, <nav> element, the page's sole navigation mechanism, line 11
findings.evidence: <nav id="nav">, containing 2 links (Plan a trip, Service alerts); no search form, sitemap link, breadcrumb trail, or related-links list appears anywhere else in the document
findings.violation: The page offers only this primary navigation menu, with no site search, sitemap link, or breadcrumb trail anywhere else in the document, and the page's own content is a general service-updates page rather than one step in a linear process, so a reader relying on anything other than already knowing this menu has no other way to reach this page or its related content.
findings.fix: Add a second, independent way to reach this page and related pages, such as a site search, a sitemap link, or a breadcrumb trail that does not merely repeat the primary navigation menu's links.

findings.evidence: <label for="phone" id="s3-form-phone-label" style="color:#cc0000">Phone number</label>; every other label in the form (Route, Email address, Promo code) uses the default text color
findings.violation: The 'Phone number' label is set apart from every other label in the form by red text color alone (#cc0000), with no accompanying text, icon, asterisk, or attribute conveying what the color distinguishes, so a reader who cannot perceive that color gets none of the information the styling is meant to carry.
findings.fix: Add a non-color signal alongside the red styling, such as label text or an icon carrying its own accessible name conveying the same distinction, or set aria-required or required on the phone input if the color is meant to mark it mandatory.

findings.evidence:
Schedule changes

, introducing a three-step 'Choose a plan / Enter payment details / Confirm your order' sequence and a form whose fields include a Promo code
findings.violation: The heading 'Schedule changes' does not describe the purchase-style wizard steps and promotional-code form that follow it, so a reader scanning headings alone cannot predict that this section contains a purchase flow rather than schedule information.
findings.fix: Give the wizard and promo-code form their own heading describing what they actually collect, or rename 'Schedule changes' to cover that content.

findings.evidence: paired with Error.
findings.violation: The promo code field is marked aria-invalid="true" but its associated error text reads only 'Error.', naming neither the field nor what is wrong with the value entered.
findings.fix: Replace the error text with one that names the field and the specific problem, for example 'Promo code is not valid or has expired.'
